A1.justification: Both complete 26-page PDFs describe the same MAPS study. Text, figures, tables, algorithms, equations and appendices support reliable comparison, including material relocated or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original PPM conversion tests, MAPS performance on SimpleCircuitEval, component ablations and case/error analyses in Tables 1–3, Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains the original PPM and MAPS evaluations, ablations and case/error analyses in Tables 1–3, Section 5 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: PPM training, synthetic circuit generation, Chain-of-Simulation, refinement, simulation-aided reasoning and fallback inference are unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 and the appendix prompt templates match.

E1.justification: Both versions use ppm-syn-lprc and the same 79-problem SimpleCircuitEval benchmark for linear pure resistive circuit analysis. No evaluated dataset, domain, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same GPT-4V, Claude-3.5, GLM-4V, Gemini-1.5, GPT-4o and GPT-4V + MMCoT comparisons and MAPS pairings. Table 3's ablated and PoT variants also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Both retain 20,000 synthetic pairs split 8:1:1, the same three PPM accuracy metrics, the 79-question benchmark and the 20-question ablation sample. Training hyperparameters and simulator settings also match.

E4.justification: The component ablations in Table 3, circuit-complexity analysis in Figure 3 and successful/error case studies are unchanged. The evaluation appendix moves from C to D without adding or removing analyses.

E5.justification: Performance reporting remains unchanged, with no added repeated-run counts, seeds, uncertainty intervals or significance tests. Table 5 retains the same descriptive dataset statistics.

E6.justification: All result entries in Tables 1–3 match, including GPT-4V + MAPS at 32.9% and ablation accuracies of 55.0%, 45.0%, 15.0% and 15.0%. Figure 3 and the appendix case/error findings are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The negative-MLE objective in Equation 1, sampling distributions in Algorithm 2 and metric definitions are retained unchanged. No theoretical assumption, derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same scientific claims about MAPS, synthetic-data training and improved circuit reasoning. The changed release statement concerns resource access rather than a scientific contribution.

C2.justification: Both retain the same interpretations of simulator dependence and perception/reasoning failures. The limitations concerning static workflow, absent simulator feedback, LPRC-only validation and broader generalization are unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces v1's promise to release code, model and dataset upon publication with a code-availability statement and repository link. Other implementation disclosures are unchanged; v2 does not separately confirm model or dataset availability.

R1.justification: Related Work moves from Section 6 to Appendix A with the same discussion and citations. The reference list and substantive positioning relative to prior research remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Related Work moves to Appendix A, the conclusion becomes Section 6, and former appendices A–C become B–D. v2 adds an acknowledgement and updates publication headers, while retaining almost all existing prose.

P2.justification: Figure 1 moves from page 3 to page 2, and Figure 5 moves from page 16 to page 15. Prompt figures are rearranged around explanatory text, with other spacing adjustments. Figure contents and table designs remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The concrete code-access link modestly improves reproducibility guidance compared with v1's future-release promise. Scientific evidence and limitations remain unchanged, and the structural edits are limited. The PDFs alone do not establish the linked repository's contents or model/data availability.
